message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1978 | **Halloween** (John Carpenter) | The original slasher that set the template for the genre. |
| 1980 | **The Shining** (Stanley Kubrick) | A psychological masterpiece based on Stephen King’s novel. |
| 1982 | **Poltergeist** (Tobe Hooper) | A chilling suburban ghost story with iconic imagery. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** (Jonathan Demme) | A tense thriller featuring Hannibal Lecter. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** (Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez) | Pioneered found‑footage horror and still feels fresh. |
| 2003 | **28 Days Later** (Danny Boyle) | A fast‑paced zombie film that revitalized the genre. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** (Oren Peli) | Low‑budget found‑footage success that sparked a franchise. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (James Wan) | A modern supernatural thriller with strong storytelling. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (Dennis Dugan) | A meta‑take that subverts horror tropes. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** (David Robert Mitchell) | A unique take on the “invisible threat” concept. |
| 2015 | **Get Out** (Jordan Peele) | A socially conscious horror that blends satire and terror. |
| 2017 | **Hereditary** (Ari Aster) | A slow‑burning dread that culminates in a shocking finale. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** (John Krasinski) | A tense, sound‑driven thriller that keeps you on edge. |
| 2020 | **Midsommar** (Ari Aster) | A daylight horror that turns the genre on its head. |
| 2021 | **The Invisible Man** (Leigh Whannell) | A modern retelling of the classic tale with a feminist twist. |
| 2022 | **Nope** (Jordan Peele) | A sci‑fi horror that mixes spectacle with social commentary. |

Feel free to pick any that match your taste—whether you prefer psychological dread, supernatural chills, or slasher thrills!
